title: Unit – 5 : Session – 9 : SLO – 2  |  Instruction Encoding and Addressing Modes
sections: I. Multiple Choice
1. B) Represent instructions in binary.
2. B) Fixed-length encoding — RISC's uniform length simplifies fetch/decode and pipelining.
3. C) How operands are accessed.
II. Fill in the Blanks
1. machine code — encoding translates assembly into binary machine code.
2. fixed — RISC uses fixed instruction length.
3. is accessed — the addressing mode specifies how an operand is accessed.
III. True or False
1. TRUE — decode complexity from encoding directly affects pipeline efficiency.
2. FALSE — variable-length instructions complicate and slow decoding.
3. TRUE.
IV. Match the Following
A) Opcode — 2) Operation to perform.
B) Operand Specifier — 3) Register/memory location info.
C) Addressing Mode — 1) How the operand is accessed.
D) Instruction Length — 4) Bits used per instruction.
V. Numerical Answers
1. 128 — 2^7 = 128 possible opcodes with a 7-bit opcode field.
2. 26 bits — 32 − 6 = 26 bits remain for operands/mode fields.
3. 32 — 2^5 = 32 registers are addressable with 5-bit specifiers.
